notes.definition: The electrons in an atom occupy the lowest available energy levels (innermost available shells). The electronic structure shows how many electrons are in each shell, for example sodium is 2,8,1.
explanation: In an atom, electrons are arranged in energy levels, also called shells, around the nucleus. Electrons occupy the lowest available energy levels first. The lowest energy level is the innermost shell, closest to the nucleus. When one shell is full, electrons start to fill the next shell out. This arrangement of electrons is called the electronic structure (or electron configuration) of the atom.

For the first 20 elements, the first shell can hold up to 2 electrons, the second shell up to 8 electrons, and the third shell holds 8 electrons before the fourth shell starts to fill. To work out the electronic structure, find the atomic number (which equals the number of electrons in an atom), then fill the shells in order: 2, then 8, then 8, then the rest. For example, sodium has 11 electrons: 2 in the first shell, 8 in the second and 1 in the third, written 2,8,1.

Electronic structures can be written as numbers separated by commas, or drawn as diagrams. In a diagram, the nucleus is shown in the centre with concentric circles for the shells, and dots or crosses for the electrons. The number of circles is the number of occupied shells, and the number of dots on each circle must match the written structure. Chlorine (17 electrons) is 2,8,7, with 7 electrons in its outer shell.

You need to be able to write the electronic structures of the first 20 elements, from hydrogen (1) to calcium (2,8,8,2). The number of occupied shells increases by one each time a new shell starts to fill, at lithium (2,1), sodium (2,8,1) and potassium (2,8,8,1). Elements whose atoms have the same number of electrons in the outer shell, such as lithium, sodium and potassium, have similar chemical properties. Helium (2), neon (2,8) and argon (2,8,8) have full outer shells, which is why they are very unreactive.
keyFacts: Electrons occupy the lowest available energy levels (innermost shells) first.
Third shell: 8 electrons before the fourth shell starts (for the first 20 elements).
In an atom, the number of electrons equals the atomic number.
The last number in the electronic structure is the number of outer-shell electrons.
The number of numbers in the electronic structure is the number of occupied shells.
Elements with the same number of outer electrons have similar chemical properties.

keyTerms.definition: A region at a specific distance from the nucleus where electrons are found.
The arrangement of electrons in the shells of an atom, written as numbers such as 2,8,1.
The highest occupied energy level, furthest from the nucleus.
The innermost shell that is not yet full; electrons go here first.
An outer shell that holds the maximum number of electrons it can, as in helium (2) and neon (2,8).

workedExamples.title: Writing an electronic structure
workedExamples.question: Write the electronic structure of aluminium (atomic number 13).
steps: Atomic number 13 means 13 electrons in the atom.

workedExamples.title: Identifying an element
workedExamples.question: An atom has the electronic structure 2,8,6. Identify the element and state how many electrons are in its outer shell.
steps: In an atom electrons = protons, so the atomic number is 16.
Atomic number 16 is sulfur. The last number, 6, is the outer-shell electrons.
workedExamples.answer: Sulfur; 6 electrons in the outer shell.

workedExamples.title: Elements 19 and 20
workedExamples.question: Write the electronic structure of potassium (atomic number 19).
steps: First shell: 2 (17 left). Second shell: 8 (9 left).
Third shell: 8 (1 left). For the first 20 elements the third shell takes 8 before the fourth starts.

misconceptions.right: In fact for the first 20 elements the third shell holds 8 before electrons go into the fourth shell, so potassium is 2,8,8,1.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often fill outer shells before inner shells are full.
misconceptions.right: In fact electrons always occupy the lowest available energy level (innermost shell) first.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often use the mass number to count electrons.
misconceptions.right: In fact the number of electrons in an atom equals the atomic number (number of protons), not the mass number.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the first shell can hold 8 electrons.
misconceptions.right: In fact the first shell holds a maximum of 2 electrons.

realWorld: Neon signs and argon-filled light bulbs use noble gases, which are unreactive because they have full outer shells.
Fireworks colours come from electrons in metal atoms moving between energy levels and giving out light of particular colours.
Semiconductor engineers choose elements such as silicon (2,8,4) and phosphorus (2,8,5) for computer chips based on their outer electrons.
examTips: Always add up your electronic structure to check it equals the atomic number.
Use the periodic table on the data sheet to find the atomic number before writing the structure.
In diagrams, draw the right number of shells and put the electrons on the circles; examiners mark the number on each shell.
Write structures with commas (2,8,1) or full stops, but keep shells in order from the nucleus outwards.
summary: Electrons occupy the lowest available energy levels first.
Shells hold 2, then 8, then 8 electrons for the first 20 elements.
Electronic structure is written like 2,8,1 or drawn as a shell diagram.
Number of electrons in an atom = atomic number.
The last number is the number of outer-shell electrons.

questions.question: What is the electronic structure of sodium (atomic number 11)?
questions.explanation: The first shell holds 2 and the second holds 8, leaving 1 electron for the third shell. 2,9 puts too many in the second shell.

questions.question: Which energy levels do electrons in an atom occupy first?
markScheme: 1 mark: the lowest available energy levels
questions.explanation: Electrons fill the lowest available energy levels, which are the innermost shells, closest to the nucleus.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of electrons in the first shell?
questions.explanation: The first shell can hold only 2 electrons. The second and third shells hold 8 for the first 20 elements.

questions.question: What is the electronic structure of oxygen (atomic number 8)?
questions.explanation: Oxygen has 8 electrons: 2 in the first shell and 6 in the second. Inner shells are always written first.

questions.question: Which element has the electronic structure 2,8,7?
questions.explanation: 2 + 8 + 7 = 17 electrons, so the atomic number is 17, which is chlorine. Fluorine is 2,7.

questions.question: What is the electronic structure of potassium (atomic number 19)?
questions.explanation: For the first 20 elements the third shell takes 8 electrons before the fourth starts, so potassium is 2,8,8,1, not 2,8,9.

questions.question: Which of these atoms has a full outer shell?
questions.explanation: 2,8,8 is argon, a noble gas with a full outer shell of 8 electrons.

questions.question: An atom has 13 protons. What is its electronic structure?
questions.explanation: 13 protons means 13 electrons in the atom: 2, then 8, then 3. This is aluminium.

questions.question: Which pair of elements have the same number of electrons in their outer shells?
questions.explanation: Lithium is 2,1 and sodium is 2,8,1, so both have 1 outer electron. Beryllium (2,2) and magnesium (2,8,2) have 2.

questions.question: Which is the correct electronic structure for calcium (atomic number 20)?
questions.explanation: Shells fill 2, 8, 8, then the remaining 2 go into the fourth shell. 2,8,10 overfills the third shell for this level, and 2,8,2,8 fills an outer shell before an inner one.

questions.question: Why does the second electron in a helium atom go into the first shell rather than the second shell?
options: The first shell is the lowest available energy level and is not yet full
The second shell can only hold one electron
The second shell is further away so it holds more electrons
Electrons repel each other so they stay as far apart as possible
markScheme: 1 mark: the first shell is the lowest available energy level and is not yet full
questions.explanation: Electrons occupy the lowest available energy level. The first shell holds up to 2, so helium's two electrons both go there (structure 2).

questions.question: Phosphorus has atomic number 15. How many electrons are in the outer shell of a phosphorus atom?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus is 2,8,5, so there are 5 outer electrons.

questions.question: An atom has the electronic structure 2,8,6. What is its atomic number?
questions.explanation: 2 + 8 + 6 = 16 electrons, and in an atom electrons = protons = atomic number. The element is sulfur.

questions.question: How many shells contain electrons in a calcium atom (atomic number 20)?
questions.explanation: Calcium is 2,8,8,2: four numbers, so four occupied shells.

questions.question: Argon has atomic number 18. How many electrons are in the third shell of an argon atom?
questions.explanation: Argon is 2,8,8, so the third shell has 8 electrons.

questions.question: Fluorine has atomic number 9. How many more electrons would a fluorine atom need to have a full outer shell?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is 2,7. The second shell holds 8, so it needs 1 more electron.

questions.question: An atom of element X has three occupied shells, and its outer shell contains 4 electrons. Calculate the atomic number of X.
markScheme: 1 mark: the inner shells must be full: 2,8,4
questions.explanation: With three shells, the first two must be full (2 and 8) because electrons fill the lowest levels first. 14 is silicon.

questions.question: Nitrogen has atomic number 7. Write the electronic structure of a nitrogen atom.
questions.explanation: 7 electrons: 2 in the first shell, 5 in the second.

questions.question:
Write the electronic structures of:
(a) magnesium (atomic number 12)
(b) aluminium (atomic number 13)
questions.explanation: Fill 2 then 8, then put the rest in the third shell.

questions.question: Identify the element with the electronic structure 2,8,8,2.
questions.explanation: 2 + 8 + 8 + 2 = 20 electrons, so the atomic number is 20: calcium.

questions.question: Explain why the electronic structure of sodium is 2,8,1 and not 2,9.
markScheme: 1 mark: the second shell can hold a maximum of 8 electrons
1 mark: so once it is full the 11th electron goes into the next (third) shell, the lowest available energy level
questions.explanation: Electrons fill the lowest available energy level, but each shell has a maximum capacity.

questions.question: Describe what a diagram of the electronic structure of a silicon atom (atomic number 14) would show.
markScheme: 1 mark: a nucleus with three shells (circles) around it
1 mark: 2 electrons in the first shell, 8 in the second and 4 in the third (2,8,4)
questions.explanation: The diagram must match the written structure 2,8,4.

questions.question: Lithium is 2,1, sodium is 2,8,1 and potassium is 2,8,8,1. State what these electronic structures have in common.
markScheme: 1 mark: each has one electron in its outer shell
questions.explanation: This is why these elements are in the same group and have similar chemical properties.

questions.question: A student writes the electronic structure of potassium (atomic number 19) as 2,8,9. Explain why this is wrong and give the correct structure.
markScheme: 1 mark: (for the first 20 elements) the third shell holds 8 electrons before the fourth shell is used
questions.explanation: The 19th electron goes into the fourth shell, giving 2,8,8,1.

questions.question: An atom has the electronic structure 2,8,5. State the number of occupied shells, the atomic number and the name of the element.
questions.explanation: Three numbers means three shells. 2 + 8 + 5 = 15 electrons, which equals the atomic number in an atom. Element 15 is phosphorus.

questions.question:
Chlorine has atomic number 17.
Describe how the electrons are arranged in a chlorine atom. In your answer, refer to energy levels and explain the order in which the shells are filled.
markScheme: Indicative content: a chlorine atom has 17 electrons (equal to the atomic number / number of protons); electrons occupy the lowest available energy levels first (innermost shells, closest to the nucleus); first shell holds 2; second shell holds 8; remaining 7 go into the third shell; electronic structure 2,8,7; 7 electrons in the outer shell; three occupied shells.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct structure 2,8,7 with a clear explanation of filling the lowest energy levels first and the shell capacities.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): correct or nearly correct structure with little explanation, or a correct statement about energy levels.
questions.explanation: Linking the number of electrons to the atomic number and then filling 2, 8, 7 gives full marks.

questions.question:
Fluorine has atomic number 9, chlorine has atomic number 17 and argon has atomic number 18.
Write the electronic structure of each element. Compare the three structures, and explain what the structures suggest about the chemical properties of these elements.
markScheme: Indicative content: fluorine 2,7; chlorine 2,8,7; argon 2,8,8; electrons fill the lowest available energy levels first, with 2 in the first shell and up to 8 in the next shells; fluorine has 2 occupied shells, chlorine and argon have 3; fluorine and chlorine both have 7 outer electrons; argon has 8 outer electrons (a full outer shell); chlorine and argon have the same number of shells but different numbers of outer electrons; elements with the same number of outer electrons have similar chemical properties, so fluorine and chlorine should react in similar ways; argon has a full outer shell so it is unreactive.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): all three structures correct, a clear comparison of shells and outer electrons, and a well-reasoned link to chemical properties.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): at least two structures correct with some comparison and a link to properties.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or more correct structures, with little comparison.
questions.explanation: Outer-shell electrons determine chemical properties, so F and Cl (7 outer electrons) are similar and Ar (full shell) is unreactive.
